signals.name: maxDepth
signals.quantity: maximum recursion depth of JSONML.parse() — count of concurrently active recursive frames
signals.storage: ThreadLocal<long[]> in fuzzing.agent.V1DepthCounters where [0]=current depth, [1]=max depth this execution
signals.reset: V1DepthCounters.reset() called in V1Guidance.getInput() before each execution
signals.read: V1DepthCounters.maxDepth() called in V1Guidance.handleResult() after each execution

plans.retention: Primary: retain inputs that achieve strictly higher maxDepth than any corpus entry. Secondary (flat signal per R46): retain inputs that are longer (growing toward input_bytes=10500) or achieve equal maxDepth with different structure. Corpus entries are prioritized by maxDepth for mutation selection (highest depth mutated 70% of the time). When maxDepth=0, retain inputs that grow in length to cross the parsing threshold. Bootstrap generates well-formed XML open tags (<X>) that immediately reach the recursive code.
mutation: XML tag block insert (25%): insert 1-to-many complete <X> open tags (3 bytes each, varied single-char tag names a-z) at a random position, with aggressive growth bias (60% of the time inserts enough to approximately double the input)

Tag-aligned chunk repetition (R45a, 30%): select a random chunk, preferring alignment to <X> tag boundaries (70% tries to start at a '<' character), and repeat it k times to grow toward MAX_INPUT_SIZE

Dictionary insert (R45b, 15%): insert a random token from the XML dictionary at a random position. Dictionary includes 26 complete open tags (<a> through <z>) plus structural tokens (<, >, /, =, </, />, <!--, -->, <?, ?>, <![CDATA[, ]]>, etc.)
Dictionary overwrite (R45b, 10%): overwrite bytes at a random position with a random dictionary token
Byte flip (6%): flip 1-8 random bits for diversity
Byte insert (5%): insert 1-4 random bytes at a random position
Byte delete (3%): delete 1-4 bytes from a random position
Byte overwrite (3%): overwrite 1-4 bytes with random values
Tag name randomization (3%): change tag names in existing <X> patterns to random letters, preserving XML structure while varying diversity
